quests.explanation: Subject (I) comes first, then the verb 'have', then the object (a car). This is the most basic English word order: who, then what they do, then what they act on.

quests.instruction: Listen closely, then rebuild the sentence in the order you hear it.
quests.hint: The word 'is' links the pointing word 'This' to the describing word.
quests.explanation: 'This' points at something, 'is' links it to the description, and 'delicious' tells us the quality. Linking sentences always follow this three-part pattern.

quests.instruction: Put the scrambled words back in the order you hear them.
quests.hint: Only one word describes how the group feels — listen for it at the end.
quests.explanation: 'We' names the group, 'are' is the plural form of 'be', and 'ready' describes their state. Short sentences like this are common in real conversation.

quests.instruction: Snap the scrambled words back into the order you hear.
quests.hint: 'My father' is one unit — don't split it apart.
quests.explanation: 'My father' (subject) + 'drives' (verb) + 'a taxi' (object) describes a job. Notice 'my father' always stays together as a single chunk.

quests.instruction: Listen closely, then rebuild the sentence in the order you hear it.
quests.hint: The place phrase 'near the school' comes after the verb, as one chunk.
quests.explanation: Subject (They) + verb (live) + place (near the school). 'Near' tells us the school is close by, not far away.

quests.instruction: Put the scrambled words back in the order you hear them.
quests.hint: This sentence gives an instruction, so there's no subject at the start — it begins with the request word.
quests.explanation: Requests like this skip the subject and start directly with 'Please' + the action (close the door), ending with the time word 'now'.

quests.instruction: Snap the scrambled words back into the order you hear.
quests.hint: 'At noon' is a fixed time chunk — the two words never separate.
quests.explanation: Subject (Our train) + verb (leaves) + time (at noon). 'At' pairs with exact clock times like noon, midnight, or six o'clock.

quests.instruction: Listen closely, then rebuild the sentence in the order you hear it.
quests.hint: 'In my bag' tells you where, and it comes last, as one group.
quests.explanation: Subject (I) + verb (keep) + object (snacks) + place (in my bag). 'In' is used because the bag is a container that holds things.
quests.textToSpeak: I keep snacks in my bag.

quests.instruction: Put the scrambled words back in the order you hear them.
quests.hint: 'Outside' is a single-word place — it sits right after the object.
quests.explanation: Subject (She) + verb (waters) + object (the plants) + place (outside). One-word place adverbs like 'outside' or 'inside' need no preposition.

quests.instruction: Snap the scrambled words back into the order you hear.
quests.hint: The describing word 'warm' sits directly before the thing it describes.
quests.explanation: In English, adjectives like 'warm' always come right before the noun: a warm jacket, never 'a jacket warm'.

quests.instruction: Listen closely, then rebuild the sentence in the order you hear it.
quests.hint: 'Fresh' describes the bread, so it stays glued to that word.
quests.explanation: Subject (My mother) + verb (bakes) + adjective + noun (fresh bread). The adjective-noun pair moves as a single unit.

quests.instruction: Put the scrambled words back in the order you hear them.
quests.hint: This time the adjective describes the subject, not the object — listen for where 'small' attaches.
quests.explanation: 'The small shop' is the subject group (with the adjective attached to 'shop'), followed by the verb (sells) and object (fruit).

quests.instruction: Snap the scrambled words back into the order you hear.
quests.hint: 'Usually' sits between the subject and the verb, not at the very start or end.
quests.explanation: Frequency adverbs like 'usually' typically go right after the subject and before the main verb: I usually walk, not usually I walk.

quests.instruction: Listen closely, then rebuild the sentence in the order you hear it.
quests.hint: 'Sometimes' comes early, but 'together' waits until the very end.
quests.explanation: Subject (We) + frequency adverb (sometimes) + verb (eat) + object (pizza) + manner (together). Two adverb-type words can appear in one sentence, in different positions.

quests.instruction: Put the scrambled words back in the order you hear them.
quests.hint: 'Never' takes the same spot 'usually' and 'sometimes' took earlier.
quests.explanation: 'Never' behaves grammatically like other frequency adverbs — it sits between the subject and the verb, even though its meaning is negative.

quests.instruction: Snap the scrambled words back into the order you hear.
quests.hint: 'His grandmother' is the whole object — the possessive word stays attached.
quests.explanation: Subject (He) + verb (calls) + object (his grandmother) + time (every week). Possessives like 'his' always come directly before the noun they own.
quests.textToSpeak: He calls his grandmother every week.

quests.instruction: Listen closely, then rebuild the sentence in the order you hear it.
quests.hint: 'Us' is a short object pronoun — it replaces a name, so it sits right after the verb.
quests.explanation: Subject (They) + verb (invite) + object pronoun (us) + reason (for dinner). Object pronouns like 'us', 'me', and 'him' always follow the verb.

quests.instruction: Put the scrambled words back in the order you hear them.
quests.hint: Two objects follow the verb here: who receives it, then what is given.
quests.explanation: 'Lend' takes two objects in this order: the person (him) comes first, then the thing given (my umbrella).

quests.instruction: Snap the scrambled words back into the order you hear.
quests.hint: 'Next to' is a two-word preposition that always stays together.
quests.explanation: Subject (Our house) + verb (is) + place (next to the park). 'Next to' means directly beside something.
quests.textToSpeak: Our house is next to the park.

quests.instruction: Listen closely, then rebuild the sentence in the order you hear it.
quests.hint: 'Under' points to a location beneath something — listen for where it attaches.
quests.explanation: Subject (The keys) + verb (are) + place (under the mat). 'Under' describes something positioned below another object.
quests.textToSpeak: The keys are under the mat.

quests.instruction: Put the scrambled words back in the order you hear them.
quests.hint: 'At the hospital' names the workplace, and it comes last.
quests.explanation: Subject (My sister) + verb (works) + place (at the hospital). 'At' is used for specific workplaces and buildings.
quests.textToSpeak: My sister works at the hospital.

quests.instruction: Snap the scrambled words back into the order you hear.
quests.hint: Two time words join together at the end: which day, then which part of the day.
quests.explanation: Subject (My flight) + verb (leaves) + time (tomorrow morning). Present simple can describe a scheduled future event, like a timetable.

quests.instruction: Listen closely, then rebuild the sentence in the order you hear it.
quests.hint: 'This weekend' names a specific time close to now.
quests.explanation: Subject (We) + verb (visit) + object (our grandparents) + time (this weekend). 'This' points to the weekend that is coming up soon.
quests.textToSpeak: We visit our grandparents this weekend.

quests.instruction: Put the scrambled words back in the order you hear them.
quests.hint: 'In ten minutes' means counting forward from now — the two number words stay together.
quests.explanation: Subject (The meeting) + verb (starts) + time (in ten minutes). 'In' with a duration means 'from now until then'.
quests.textToSpeak: The meeting starts in ten minutes.

quests.instruction: Snap the scrambled words back into the order you hear.
quests.hint: This is a question, so the small helper word jumps to the very front, before the subject.
quests.explanation: Questions with 'can' move the auxiliary in front of the subject: Can you...? instead of You can... This word order signals a request.

quests.instruction: Listen closely, then rebuild the sentence in the order you hear it.
quests.hint: Listen for the question word right at the start — it comes before 'you', not after.
quests.explanation: Yes/no questions in present simple begin with 'Do' or 'Does', then the subject, then the base verb: Do you need...?

quests.instruction: Put the scrambled words back in the order you hear them.
quests.hint: The question word 'Where' leads, then the verb 'is' follows immediately after it.
quests.explanation: Wh-questions start with the question word (Where), followed by the verb (is), then the subject (the nearest bank).

quests.instruction: Snap the scrambled words back into the order you hear.
quests.hint: 'Before dinner' tells you the order of two events — it comes after the main action.
quests.explanation: Subject (I) + verb (finish) + object (my homework) + time clause (before dinner). 'Before' shows which event happens first.
quests.textToSpeak: I finish my homework before dinner.

quests.instruction: Listen closely, then rebuild the sentence in the order you hear it.
quests.hint: A number word and a describing word both sit in front of 'drinks' — in that order.
quests.explanation: Subject (The waiter) + verb (brings) + quantity + adjective + noun (two cold drinks). Numbers come before adjectives, which come before the noun.
quests.textToSpeak: The waiter brings two cold drinks.

quests.instruction: Put the scrambled words back in the order you hear them.
quests.hint: Two actions are joined by 'and' — listen for where the second action begins.
quests.explanation: Subject (We) + verb 1 (pack our bags) + 'and' + verb 2 (leave early). 'And' links two actions done by the same subject, in the order they happen.
quests.textToSpeak: We pack our bags and leave early.
